subject: Cloud Computing
title: AWS Launches and Changes Everything
description: A fast breakdown of AWS Launches and Changes Everything for builders.

hook.text: On March 14, 2006, Amazon launched S3 — simple online storage. The cloud era began.

buildup.text: Months later, EC2 let anyone rent virtual servers by the hour. No contracts, no hardware.

discovery.text: Startups could launch with zero upfront infrastructure cost. Just a credit card.

twist.text: AWS didn't target enterprises first. It targeted scrappy startups nobody else served.

climax.text: Those startups grew into Netflix, Airbnb, and Slack — all built on AWS.

punchline.text: AWS bet on startups. The startups bet on everything.

quiz.question: What was the first AWS service launched in 2006?
options: S3, a simple online storage service
EC2, a virtual server rental service

details.summary: AWS launched S3 in March 2006 and EC2 in August 2006, giving anyone with a credit card access to scalable storage and computing. Startups that previously needed to buy servers could now launch products in minutes, democratizing infrastructure access globally.
details.whyItMatters: AWS's launch made infrastructure accessible to anyone, eliminating the capital barrier to starting a tech company. It fundamentally changed how software is built and deployed.
takeaways: S3 launched in March 2006, EC2 in August 2006
A credit card replaced the need for hardware purchases
Startups could now launch products in minutes, not months

faq.question: What were S3 and EC2?
faq.answer: S3, Simple Storage Service, provided scalable object storage priced per gigabyte. EC2, Elastic Compute Cloud, offered resizable virtual servers billed by the hour. Together, they provided the two fundamental building blocks of cloud computing: storage and compute.

faq.question: How did AWS change the startup world?
faq.answer: Before AWS, startups needed tens of thousands of dollars for servers before writing any code. AWS eliminated capital expenditure, letting founders start with a few dollars a month. This dramatically lowered the barrier to entry and accelerated the pace of innovation.
